title: Temple of Portunus
source: Two ordinary exterior pictures and the pinned standard PMTiles/Mapzen extract.
axis: +X east;+Y up;+Z south. Internal architectural+Z faces north-northwest at the mapped stair.
identityStatus: Q849241/way251331418 identifies the exact temple. Twenty-two PMTiles building components retain their original vertices: main outline, U-shaped cella wall, podium, eleven stair parts, column bases, all18 shafts and roof/entablature bands. The mapped stair projection and ordinary front picture fix the north-northwest front; the rear photograph confirms four engaged rear columns. reconstruction.scope: Specific present-day Temple of Portunus exterior: high mapped podium and eleven front stair parts, six free-standing Ionic portico columns, twelve engaged side/rear columns, roofed pronaos, closed recessed cella door, layered entablature, front/rear triangular pediments and complete shallow tiled gable roof. The neighboring Temple of Hercules Victor, church and modern street buildings remain independent.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Standard-map parts provide podium3m, shaft interval3.2–10m, cella10m, cornice11–11.5m and roof envelope11.5–12.9m. The model follows these approximate heights above the declared lower datum, with fluted shafts ending9.65m and coarse Ionic capitals rising10.25m. Ordinary pictures guide cornice tiers, roof pitch, fluting, closed door and capitals; exact ornament, wall repairs and thresholds are not surveyed.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: The original161-square/6m standard Mapzen/USGS grid remains unchanged. The lower datum is the least offset that keeps every mapped stair top0.2m above the actual rendered terrain directly beneath its footprint. Each intersecting native triangle is clipped to the footprint and its linear height evaluated at every resulting corner. The3m upper podium and all higher treads cover their original coarse grade; retaining faces extend below the minimum local terrain. Numerical clipping scraps under0.1 square metres are omitted from the upper floor, removing false stair-side spikes; all original mapped controls remain intact. No ground or water cutout. Surrounding ground remains native; exact archaeological levels remain approximate.

nativeTerrainClearance.basis: Every rendered native triangle intersecting each occupied floor is clipped to that footprint. Linear terrain height reaches its maximum at a clipped corner, so evaluating all such corners proves the opaque floor stays above the original terrain. Repeated corners are counted as checks, not unique vertices.
